data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when the subject has no independent path to pass the test except by satisfying a condition the test itself installs; in the record, the 'shown-to-fail-first' ritual installs a guard before the mutation can be observed, so the 3-of-26 result is not a measurement of mutation survival but a measurement of how many mutations were planted after the guard was already in place.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If mutations were planted before the shown-to-fail-first installation, the order would be reversed and the test could constrain the mutation directly.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the guard were removed and the test still passed, the test would be describing the mutation rather than constraining it.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3-of-26 result were replicated across different repositories with different authors, the installation-order confound would be weakened.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Shown-to-fail-first installation changes the order of operations: the test is made to fail against the mutated code before the guard is introduced, so the guard's presence is a precondition for the test's later passage. The test then describes the guard's installation state rather than constraining the mutation.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
